page.description: Ventoy editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A tool that turns one USB stick into a boot menu for image files: copy ISO, WIM, IMG and VHD files onto it and Ventoy boots them directly, without rewriting the stick for each one.
pros: Many images on one stick, each booted from a menu without reflashing.
Images are plain files, so adding or removing one is a file copy.
UEFI and legacy BIOS boot, on x86 and ARM64 builds.
Free and open source, with signed releases and a published SHA-256 list.
cons: It is a boot loader, not an operating system of its own.
Secure Boot needs the project's key enrolled once (MOK).
Some images boot only with extra settings or a different Ventoy mode.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Ventoy; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Install Ventoy to a USB stick once (from the Linux archive or the live CD), then copy image files onto it. Installing erases the whole stick; copying images afterwards does not.

editions.name: Live CD image
editions.description: A bootable image of the Ventoy installer, for machines where running the Linux archive is not practical.
editions.usbNote: 187 MB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Linux installer archive
editions.description: The installer for Linux, run from an unpacked archive to write Ventoy to a stick.
editions.usbNote: 20 MB archive. Unpack it and run Ventoy2Disk.sh against the target stick; writing erases the stick.
